h: Moshe's Gift of Shabbos and the Perfection of Faith
The Shabbos gift reflects Moshe’s exceptional humility: even at the summit of wisdom, he ascribed all attainment to Hashem and stood in complete emunah.
The Gift of Shabbos: Truth and Faith

p: יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ כִּי עֶבֶד נֶאֱמָן קָרָאתָ לּוֹ.
'Moshe shall rejoice in the gift of his portion, for You called him a faithful servant.'

בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ הוּא הַשַּׁבָּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוּ עפ"י המ"ר (פ' שְׁמוֹת) שֶׁבֵּירֵר הַשַּׁבָּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִצְרַיִם וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לפי"ז מ"ש כִּי עֶבֶד נֶאֱמָן קָרָאתָ לּוֹ אֵיזֶהוּ קִישּׁוּר י"ל דְּמַשְׁמַע דְּזֶה טַעַם שֶׁיִּשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַשַּׁבָּת.

'The gift of his portion' refers to Shabbos, as the Midrash Rabbah (Parashas Shemos) is understood to teach: in Egypt Moshe selected Shabbos for Israel. If so, how is 'for You called him a faithful servant' connected? The wording suggests that his faithfulness is precisely the reason he rejoices in the gift of Shabbos.
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן דְּאִי' בְּרַעַ"מ (זח"ג רל"א) אִיהוּ אֱמֶת וְאִיהִי אֱמוּנָה וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אע"ה אֱמֶת.
The matter is that Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar III, 231) teaches, 'He is truth and she is faith.' The attribute of Yaakov Avinu is truth.
שֶׁלּוֹ הֵאִיר הַיִּחוּד בְּמִדַּת אֱמֶת שֶׁיָּהּ מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הוי"ה שֶׁמּוֹרֶה אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם.
For in Yaakov the Divine unity shone as truth: he became a vehicle for the Name Havayah, indicating, 'You were He before the world was created, and You are He after the world was created.'
וְהַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁהֵם כנס"י אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה שֶׁלָּהֶם הֵאִיר עַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה שֶׂה' אֶחָד.
But for the tribes, who embody the community of Israel, 'she is faith'; the recognition of Hashem's oneness shines in them through emunah.
ועז"א (פְּסָחִים נו.) שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים ליע"א כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד כֵּן אֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ אֶלָּא אֶחָד.
This is what the Gemara (Pesachim 56a) means when it says that the tribes told Yaakov: 'Just as in your heart there is only One, so in our hearts there is only One.'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁאַתָּה מַכִּיר זֶה הַיִּחוּד בְּמִדַּת אֱמֶת כָּךְ אֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ תְּפִיסָה בְּשֵׁם הוי"ה.
That is, just as your heart recognizes divine unity through truth, so too our hearts contain only the One, though we cannot directly grasp the Divine Name Havayah.
דְּשָׁם זֶה אֵינוֹ נָהֲגָה בעוה"ז מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁיֵּשׁ כֹּחוֹת אֲחֵרִים וּבְחִירָה.
That Name is not pronounced as written in this world, since to the eye there appear to be other powers and human free choice.
ומ"מ עַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה אָנוּ מַאֲמִינִים שֶׂה' אֶחָד כְּמוֹ קֹודֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה כֵּן בעוה"ז.
Nevertheless, through faith we affirm that Hashem is One just as He was before the creation of the world, even though this is not manifest to the eye in the present world.
וז"ש בגמ' בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה פָּתַח יע"א וְאָמַר בשכמל"ו שֶׁזֶּה מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁמַּכִּירִין מַלְכוּתוֹ יָת' וְשֵׁם הוי"ה נָהֲגָה עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם אֵד' שֶׁנִּקְרָא בָּאד'.

Thus the Gemara says that Yaakov then began to recite, 'Blessed is the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever.' This expresses Malchus: recognition of His kingship. The written Name Havayah is pronounced through the Name Adnus.
וְזֶהוּ אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה בְּחֵי' כנס"י.
This is the meaning of 'she is faith,' the aspect of the community of Israel.
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא יוֹם ז' מִדַּת מַלְכוּת כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And Shabbos, the seventh day, corresponds to the attribute of Malchus, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 1:28: “Alternatively, “he saw their burdens,” – he saw that they had no respite. He went and said to Pharaoh: ‘One who has a slave, if he does not rest one day a week, he will die. These are your slaves. If you do not allow them to rest one day a week they will die.’ He said to him: ‘Go and do with them whatever you say.’ Moses went and instituted the day of Shabbat for rest. “He saw an Egyptian man.” What did he see? Rav Huna said in the name of bar Kapara: Because of four matters, Israel was redeemed from Egypt: One, because they did not change their names. From where is it derived that they were not suspected of licentiousness? The fact is that there was one woman and the verse publicized her, as it is stated: “[The son of an Israelite woman and he was the son of an Egyptian man]…and the name of his mother was Shelomit bat Divri….” (Leviticus 24: 10–11). Our Sages, of blessed memory, say: The taskmasters were Egyptian and the foremen were Israelite; one taskmaster was appointed over ten foremen, and one foreman was appointed over ten Israelites. The taskmasters would go to the homes of the foremen early in the morning to get them out to work with the crowing of the rooster. Once, an Egyptian taskmaster went to an Israelite foreman and directed his glance to his wife, who was beautiful and flawless. He arrived there at the time of the crowing of the rooster and got him out of the house. The Egyptian returned and consorted with his wife, as she thought it was her husband, and she was impregnated. Her husband returned and saw the Egyptian emerging from his home. He asked her: ‘Did he touch you?’ She said: ‘Yes, and I thought he was you.’ Once the taskmaster realized that [the Israelite] had sensed what he had done, he returned him to hard labor, and was beating him, seeking to kill him. Moses was looking at him and watching him, and he saw by means of the Divine Spirit what he had done at his home and saw what he was going to do to him in the field. He said: ‘This one is certainly liable for execution, as it is written: “One who strikes a person shall be put to death” (Leviticus 24:21). Moreover, he consorted with Datan’s wife and for that he is liable for execution, as it is stated: “The adulterer and the adulteress shall be put to death”’ (Leviticus 20:10). That is what is written: “He turned this way and that [and saw that there was no man; he smote the Egyptian and concealed him in the sand]” (Exodus 2:12) – he saw what he had done to him in the house and what he had done to him in the field.”

p: וְהִנֵּה במ"ר (פ' בְּרָכָה) דָּרַשׁ עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ וְאַתְּ עָלִית עַל כֻּולָּנָה שֶׁנִּתְעַלָּה יוֹתֵר מִן הַכֹּל וְחָשַׁב שָׁם שֶׁנִּתְעַלָּה יוֹתֵר מֵהָאָבוֹת וְאַפֵּי' מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת ע"ש.

Yet the Midrash Rabbah (Parashas Vezos HaBerachah) applies to Moshe the verse 'And you rise above them all': he surpassed everyone, including the patriarchs and even Yaakov Avinu, whose attribute is truth.
וְנִקְרָא אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים וְאִי' (במד"ת בְּרָכָה) כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם גּוֹזֵר עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ כו' וּכְ' שָׁם בְּכִינּוּי.
Moshe is called 'the man of God,' and the Midrash Tanchuma on Vezos HaBerachah speaks of his authority in an analogy to a person who issues a decree to his wife, using an indirect formulation.

הקב"ה גָּזַר עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעָשָׂה וְהַכַּוָּנָה לְהֵיפֶךְ כִּבְיָכוֹל וְכָאן אָמַר יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַשַּׁבָּת וְיִקְשֶׁה הָא מַדְרֵגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ מְעֻולֶּה אַף מִמַּדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב אע"ה שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת וְאֵיךְ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁמַּתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת בְּחֵי' אֱמוּנָה ועז"א כִּי עֶבֶד נֶאֱמָן קָרָאתָ לּוֹ וְהוּא מש"נ לֹא כֵן עַבְדִּי מֹשֶׁה בְּכָל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמַר הוּא.

The Holy One decreed and Moshe acted—or, figuratively, the reverse. Why, then, when Moshe's level exceeds even Yaakov's attribute of truth, do we call Shabbos, associated with faith, the gift of his portion? The answer is: 'For You called him a faithful servant,' as Scripture says, 'Not so My servant Moshe; in all My house he is faithful' (Numbers 12:7).

שֶׁהוּא נִשְׁלַם בְּמִדַּת אֱמוּנָה מֵהֵימָנוּתָא שְׁלִימְתָּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא בגמ' אֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה כמ"ש (תָּמִיד כח.) יַחְזִיק בֶּאֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עֵינַי בְּנֶאֶמְנֵי אֶרֶץ לָשֶׁבֶת עִמָּדִי וְהוּא מִדַּת דהמע"ה שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת וְזֶה נִקְרָא נֶאֱמָן שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּמִדַּת אֱמוּנָה מֵהֵימָנוּתָא שְׁלִימְתָּא וזש"נ לָשֶׁבֶת עִמָּדִי עד"ש (יוֹמָא כה.) אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בָּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד.

Moshe was perfected in the attribute of emunah, complete fidelity. The Gemara calls this 'additional faith,' as Tamid 28a says: 'Let him hold firmly to abundant faith,' citing, 'My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with Me.' This is the attribute of David HaMelech, vehicle of Malchus. Such a person is called faithful, having perfected complete faith. 'To dwell with Me' recalls Yoma 25a: no one may sit in the Temple courtyard except kings of the House of David.
אָמְנָם זֶהוּ מַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אַף שֶׁמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ הָיָה מְעֻולֶּה מְאֹד וְאַף מִמִּדַּת יַעֲקֹב אע"ה שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת.
Precisely here lies Moshe's greatness, notwithstanding how exalted he was, even above the level of Yaakov whose attribute was truth.
וְזֶה סוֹד מש"נ וּתְמוּנַת הוי"ה יַבִּיט.
This is the secret of the verse, 'He beholds the likeness of Hashem' (Numbers 12:8).
דְּצוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא.
For Yaakov's image is engraved upon the Throne.
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב הָיָה כאדה"ר קֹודֶם הַקִּלְקוּל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ כ"פ.
Yaakov resembled Adam HaRishon before his corruption, as we have explained repeatedly.
וּבַגְּמָ' (ב"ר פד.) אִי' שֻׁופְרֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב מֵעֵין שֻׁופְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן ובזוה"ק (ח"א קמב ב וש"מ) אִי' דְּשֻׁופְרֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב שֻׁופְרֵיהּ דְּאָדָם הֲוָה ע"ש.
The Midrash states that Yaakov's beauty was like Adam HaRishon's beauty; likewise the Zohar (I, 142b, and elsewhere) says that Yaakov's beauty was Adam's beauty.
וְהוּא דְּמוּת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא דִּכְתִיב נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ.
He is the human likeness above the Throne, as Scripture says, 'Let us make man in Our image, after Our likeness.'
וְזֶהוּ תְּמוּנַת הוי"ה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אע"ה מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הוי"ה.
This is 'the likeness of Havayah': Yaakov was a vehicle for the Name Havayah.
וּבְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ כִּיתִב וּתְמוּנַת ה' יַבִּיט וְאָמְרוּ (ב"ר פ' מד) אֵין הַבָּטָה אֶלָּא מִלְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה (ונת' בִּקְדֻושַּׁת שַׁבָּת רֵישׁ מא' ז).

Concerning Moshe it says, 'He beholds the likeness of Hashem'; and Bereishis Rabbah (chapter 44) teaches that 'beholding' is from above downward, as explained at the beginning of Kedushas Shabbos, discourse 7.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּעֲלָתוֹ גָּבוֹהַּ מִמַּעֲלַת יעאע"ה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ עָלָיו וְאַתְּ עָלִית עַל כֻּולָּנָה.
This indicates that Moshe's rank surpassed even Yaakov's, as the Midrash applied to him, 'You rise above them all.'
ומ"מ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁהָיָה עָנוּ מִכָּל הָאָדָם הֶחֱזִיק עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא נֶאֱמָן בְּמִדַּת אֱמוּנָה שֶׁאַף שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ גָּבוֹהַּ.
Nevertheless Moshe, the humblest of all people, considered himself faithful in the attribute of emunah, even though he knew his spiritual level was very high.
הָיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁאֵין זֶה רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּחַר בּוֹ השי"ת לִשְׁלֹוחַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְקַבֵּל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל כֵּן הִגְדִּיל מַעֲלָתוֹ.
He would say that his level was only because the Blessed One had chosen him to be sent to Israel and to receive the Torah, and so had elevated him.

וְהוּא רַק כְּדִמְיוֹן הַטָּלֶה שֶׁיָּצָא עֲשִׂירִי שֶׁנִּתְקַדֵּשׁ בִּקְדֻושַּׁת מַעֲשֵׂר עַל יְדֵי שֶׁסֻּוקָּר אוֹתוֹ בְּסִקְרָא שֶׁאֵין זֶה כְּלָל מִצִּדּוֹ שֶׁהֲרֵי מֻוכְרָח לִהְיוֹת א' יוֹצֵא עֲשִׂירִי כֵּן נִצְרָךְ א' לִהְיוֹת נִבְחָר לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְנִבְחַר הוּא מהשי"ת וְאִם הָיָה רְצוֹן השי"ת הָיָה בּוֹחֵר בְּאַחֵר וְזֶה מש"נ בְּכָל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמָן הוּא.

It is like the lamb that happens to emerge tenth and is sanctified as ma'aser when marked with red: its sanctity does not arise from any merit of its own, for one animal had to be tenth. Similarly, someone had to be chosen to receive the Torah, and Moshe was chosen by Hashem. Had He wished, He could have selected another. This is 'in all My house he is faithful.'

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: Yet the Midrash Rabbah (Parashas Vezos HaBerachah) applies to Moshe the verse 'And you rise above them all': he surpassed everyone, including the patriarchs and even Yaakov Avinu, whose attribute is truth.

paragraphs.text: Devarim Rabbah 11:3: ““This is the blessing” – that is what the verse said: “Many women have performed valiantly, but you have surpassed them all” (Proverbs 31:29). What is, “but you have surpassed them all”? It is speaking of Moses, because he was exalted over them all. How so? Adam the first man says to Moses: ‘I am greater than you, as I was created in the image of the Holy One blessed be He.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “God created man in His own image” (Genesis 1:27). Moses says to him: ‘I am more exalted than you, as you, the glory that was given to you was taken from you, as it is stated: “Man [Adam] does not abide in honor” (Psalms 49:13). But I, the radiance of my face that the Holy One blessed be He gave me, it remains with me.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “His eye had not dimmed, and his vitality had not departed” (Deuteronomy 34:7). Another matter, Noah said to Moses: ‘I am greater than you, as I was delivered from the generation of the Flood.’ Moses said to him: ‘I am more exalted than you, as you saved yourself, but you did not have the ability to save your generation. But I saved myself and saved my generation when they incurred liability to be eradicated due to the [sin of the Golden] Calf.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “The Lord reconsidered the evil that He had spoken of doing to His people” (Exodus 32:14). To what is the matter comparable? It is to two ships that were at sea, and there were two captains in them. One saved himself but did not save his ship, and one saved himself and his ship. Whom do they laud? Is it not the one who saved himself and his ship? So, Noah saved only himself, but Moses saved himself and his generation. That is, “but you have surpassed them all.” Another matter, Abraham said to Moses: ‘I am greater than you, as I would provide sustenance to the passersby.’ Moses said to him: ‘I am more exalted than you, as you would provide sustenance for uncircumcised people, but I provided sustenance for circumcised people. Moreover, you would provide sustenance in the settled area, and I would provide sustenance in the wilderness.’ Isaac said to Moses: ‘I am greater than you as I extended my neck upon the altar and saw the countenance of the Divine Spirit.’ Moses said to him: ‘I am more exalted than you, as you saw the countenance of the Divine Presence and your eyes dimmed.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is written: “It was when Isaac was old, his eyes dimmed from seeing” (Genesis 27:1). What is “from seeing”? It is from seeing the Divine Presence. ‘But I would speak with the Divine Presence face to face and my eyes did not dim.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “Moses did not know that the skin of his face was radiant” (Exodus 34:29). Jacob said to Moses: ‘I am greater than you, as I encountered the angel and overcame him.’ Moses said to him: ‘You encountered the angel in your environment, but I ascended to them in their environment, and they fear me.’ From where is it derived? It is as it is stated: “The kings of armies [malkhei tzevaot] flee again and again…” (Psalms 68:13). That is why Solomon said: “Many women have performed valiantly, [but you have surpassed them all].” The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Since he was exalted above everyone, he will bless Israel’ – “this is the blessing.””

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 44:12: ““He took him outside, and said: Look now to the heavens, and count the stars, if you can count them, and He said to him: So will your offspring be” (Genesis 15:5). “He took him outside” – Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in the name of Rabbi Levi: Did He take him outside the world, that the verse should say: “He took him outside [haḥutza]”? Rather, he showed him the streets of the heavens, just as it says: “While He had not yet made earth and the outer ranges [ḥutzot]” (Proverbs 8:26). Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He took him up above the dome of the heavens. That is what He said to him: “Look [habet] now to the heavens” – [the expression] habata refers only to looking from above to below. The Rabbis say: [God told him:] ‘You are a prophet, not an astrologer,’ as it is stated: “Now, restore the man's wife, as he is a prophet” (Genesis 20:7). In the days of Jeremiah, Israel sought to adopt this mindset, but the Holy One blessed be He did not allow them to do so. That is what is written: “So said the Lord: Do not learn the way of the nations, and from the signs of the heavens do not fear…” (Jeremiah 10:2) – your forefather Abraham sought to adopt that mindset, but I did not allow him to do so. Rabbi Levi said: [The saying goes:] While your sandal is on your foot, trample the thorns. Anyone who is situated below them [the stars] fears them, but you, who are situated above them, trample them. Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: There are three things that can annul evil decrees, and they are: Prayer, charity, and repentance. And the three of them are stated in one verse. That is what is written: “My people upon whom My name is called humble themselves, and pray” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is prayer; “and seek My presence” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is charity, as you say: “I shall encounter Your presence through charity” (Psalms 17:15); “and repent from their evil ways” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is repentance. And following these, “I will forgive their sin and will heal their land” (II Chronicles 7:14). Rabbi Huna bar Rav Yosef said: Change of name and a good deed also [can annul evil decrees.] Change of name, we learn from Abraham: “Your name will no longer be called Abram” (Genesis 17:5). A good deed, we learn from the people of Nineveh, as it is stated: “God saw their actions, that they turned away [from their evil ways, and God relented of the disaster that he had said]…” (Jonah 3:10). Some say: Change of location, as well, as it is stated: “The Lord said to Abram: Go you [from your land]” (Genesis 12:1). Rabbi Muna said: A fast as well, as it is stated: “May the Lord answer you on a day of trouble” (Psalms 20:2). Rava bar Maḥasya and Rabbi Ḥama ben Guryon said in the name of Rav: A fast is as effective against a [bad] dream as fire is against chaff. Rav Yosef said: [Only if the fast is done] on that same day, even if it is on Shabbat.”

Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: There are three things that can annul evil decrees, and they are: Prayer, charity, and repentance. And the three of them are stated in one verse. That is what is written: “My people upon whom My name is called humble themselves, and pray” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is prayer; “and seek My presence” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is charity, as you say: “I shall encounter Your presence through charity” (Psalms 17:15); “and repent from their evil ways” (II Chronicles 7:14) – this is repentance. And following these, “I will forgive their sin and will heal their land” (II Chronicles 7:14). Rabbi Huna bar Rav Yosef said: Change of name and a good deed also [can annul evil decrees.] Change of name, we learn from Abraham: “Your name will no longer be called Abram” (Genesis 17:5). A good deed, we learn from the people of Nineveh, as it is stated: “God saw their actions, that they turned away [from their evil ways, and God relented of the disaster that he had said]…” (Jonah 3:10). Some say: Change of location, as well, as it is stated: “The Lord said to Abram: Go you [from your land]” (Genesis 12:1). Rabbi Muna said: A fast as well, as it is stated: “May the Lord answer you on a day of trouble” (Psalms 20:2). Rava bar Maḥasya and Rabbi Ḥama ben Guryon said in the name of Rav: A fast is as effective against a [bad] dream as fire is against chaff. Rav Yosef said: [Only if the fast is done] on that same day, even if it is on Shabbat.”

paragraphs.text: Mesillas Yesharim 22:9–12: “A person of sound understanding, even if he has merited to be a truly great and exceptional sage, will see, upon examining and reflecting, that there is no place for pride or self-exaltation. A person endowed with an intellect that knows more than others is doing only what his natural constitution enables him to do: like a bird that soars because this is its nature, or an ox that pulls with its strength because that is its constitution. Likewise, a sage is wise because his nature leads him to this. If the person who is now less wise possessed the same natural intellect, he would become wise just as this person has. There is therefore no reason for self-exaltation or pride. Rather, if he possesses much wisdom, he is obligated to teach it to those who need it, as Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said in Avos 2:9: “If you have learned much Torah, do not claim credit for yourself, for this is what you were created for.” If he is wealthy, he should rejoice in his portion and help those who lack; if he is strong, he should assist those who falter and rescue the oppressed. To what is this comparable? To the servants of a household, each appointed over a particular matter. Each should stand at his post according to his assignment, to complete the household's work and its needs. In truth there is no room here for pride.”

p: וְזֶה מ"ש בזוה"ק פ' זוֹ (עו א) אַחַר שֶׁאָמַר יְהַב חָכְמְתָא עִלָּאָה לאדה"ר וְאַחַר כָּךְ קִלְקֵל.
Zohar on this parashah (I, 76a) relates how supernal wisdom was given to Adam HaRishon, but afterward Adam caused damage.
אָמַר יְהַב חָכְמְתָא לְנֹחַ וּלְפַח בָּהּ לקב"ה.
It then says that wisdom was given to Noach, but he sinned with it before the Holy One.

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא רָצָה לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם אדה"ר וכמ"ש (בזוה"ק לְעֵיל עג סע"א) כַּד בְּעָא נֹחַ לְמִבְדַּק בְּהַהוּא חוֹבָא דְּבָדַק אדה"ר לָאו לְאִתְדַּבְּקָא בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא לְמַנְדַּע וּלְאִתַּקְנָא עָלְמָא וְלָא יְכִיל ע"ש.

Noach sought to repair Adam's sin, as the Zohar earlier (73a) says: when Noach sought to examine the same transgression Adam had examined, he did not wish to attach himself to it but to understand and rectify the world; yet he could not.
וז"ש לְבָתַר מַה כְּתִיב וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן הַיַּיִן וַיִּשְׁכָּר וְכוּ' וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִכִּיר מַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ הַחָכְמָה וְחָשַׁב שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְתַקֵּן פְּגָם שֶׁל אדה"ר.
Therefore the Zohar continues, 'Afterward what is written? He drank of the wine and became drunk.' He became conscious of the lofty wisdom granted him and imagined that he could repair Adam's damage.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר יְהַב חָכְמְתָא לְאַבְרָהָם וּפְלַח בָּהּ לקב"ה לְבָתַר נָפֵיק מִנֵּיהּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְכֵן יִצְחָק נָפֵיק מִנֵּיהּ עֵשָׂו.
Then the Zohar says that wisdom was given to Avraham, who served Hashem with it, but afterward Yishmael came from him; and Yitzchak, from whom Esav emerged.
וְאַף דְּאִי' (נְדָרִים לא.) בְּיִצְחָק וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק.
Admittedly Nedarim 31a states, 'Through Yitzchak,' but not all of Yitzchak's descendants are included.
אַךְ הַכַּוָּנָה מַה דְּכ' וַיֵּרַע הַדָּבָר מְאֹד בְּעֵינֵי אַבְרָהָם עַל אוֹדֹת בְּנוֹ.
Rather, the point is in the verse, 'The matter was very displeasing to Avraham concerning his son' (Bereishis 21:11).
וְזֶה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה עִלָּאָה שֶׁנִּיתַּן לאאע"ה הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי אֵין פְּסֹולֶת בְּזַרְעוֹ וְאַף יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא טוֹב וע"כ וַיֵּרַע הַדָּבָר וְגוֹ'.
Because of the supreme wisdom granted him, Avraham supposed there could be no defective element among his offspring, and that even Yishmael was good; therefore the matter grieved him deeply.
וְכֵן בְּיִצְחָק נֶחְשָׁב מש"נ וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו.
Similarly, with Yitzchak Scripture says, 'Yitzchak loved Esav.'
וְזֶה הָיָה ג"כ מִטַּעַם זֶה שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא מִצִּדּוֹ נִשְׁלַם כָּל כָּךְ בְּוַדַּאי גַּם עֵשָׂו טוֹב.
He too reasoned that since he himself had attained such perfection, Esav must surely be good as well.
וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ יַעֲקֹב נְסַב תְּרֵין אַחָתָן.
The Zohar then says, 'Yaakov took two sisters.'
וְהִקְשָׁה בִּנְצוּצֵי אוֹרוֹת הָא בְּרֵישׁ תְּרוּמָה מַשְׁמַע שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב מֻוכְרָח לִישָּׂא ב' אֲחָיוֹת עַל פִּי הַסּוֹד ע"ש.
The commentary Nitzotzei Oros asks: the beginning of Zohar Terumah implies that by the mystical order Yaakov was required to marry two sisters.

וּלְפִי הָאָמוּר י"ל בְּשֶׁאַמַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הוי"ה וְצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בכה"כ הָיָה רָאוּי לוֹ לִישָּׂא הַב' אֲחָיוֹת עפ"י הַסּוֹד אַךְ עכ"פ הוּא שֶׁנָּשָׂא ב' הָאֲחָיוֹת יָדַע מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הוי"ה וְזֶה נֶחְשָׁב לוֹ לְחִסָּרוֹן.

According to this explanation, we may say that Yaakov, a vehicle for the Name Havayah whose image is engraved upon the Throne, was indeed suited to marry the sisters according to the mystery. Nevertheless, by doing so he was conscious of the greatness of his own spiritual rank, and that awareness was counted as a deficiency.
וְחָשַׁב שֶׁבְּכֻולָּם הִזִּיק מַה שֶׁנִּמְסַר לָהֶם הַחָכְמָה.
The Zohar thus considers how, in each case, the granting of wisdom entailed some detriment.
משא"כ בְּמֹשֶׁה אָמַר יְהַב חָכְמְתָא לְמֹשֶׁה מַה כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ בְּכָל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמָן הוּא.
But of Moshe it says: 'He gave wisdom to Moshe'; and what is written of him? 'In all My house he is faithful.'
וְלָא הֲוָה כְּמֹשֶׁה שַׁמָּשׁ מְהֵימָן בְּכִלְהוּ דַּרְגִין כו' אֶלָּא קָאֵים בְּמֵהִימְנוּתָא עִלָּאָה כִּדְקָא יָאוּת.
'None was like Moshe, who served faithfully on every level ... rather, he stood in supernal faith as was fitting.'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁבְּכָל מַעֲלַת מַדְרֵגָתוֹ לֹא יָדַע מְאוּמָה וְהֶחֱזִיק עַצְמוֹ שׁוֹהֵא רַק בִּבְחִי' אֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה וְכָאָמוּר.
For, as we have explained, despite every greatness of his station, he regarded it as nothing attributable to himself and held himself only in the aspect of abundant emunah.

וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ יְהַב חָכְמְתָא לִשְׁלֹמֹה מַלְכָּא לְבָתַר כו' אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה אָתֵי אֵל וְחָכְמְתָא דִּילֵיהּ וְאוֹכַל וְאֵיכוֹל לוֹ עֲבַד רְעוּתִי וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶׁאָמַר אֲנִי אַרְבֶּה וְלֹא אָסוּר (כמ"ש סַנְהֶדְרִין כא:) וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּמְסַר לוֹ הַחָכְמְתָא עִלָּאָה וְעָלָיו יֵשׁ מ"ד בגמ' (ר"ה כא:) וְלֹא קָם נָבִיא וְגוֹ' כְּמֹשֶׁה בַּנְּבִיאִים לֹא קָם בִּמְלָכִים קָם וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר אָתֵי אֵל וְחָכְמְתָא דִּילֵיהּ אָמַר אֲנִי אַרְבֶּה וְלֹא אָסוּר.

The Zohar then relates that wisdom was given to King Shlomo. Shlomo said, in effect, 'God and His wisdom are with me, and I can act as I wish,' corresponding to 'I shall increase [wives] and will not stray' (Sanhedrin 21b). This confidence came from his supernal wisdom. One view in Rosh Hashanah 21b says that 'no prophet arose like Moshe' excludes prophets, but one did arise among kings; nevertheless Shlomo relied upon that wisdom and declared, 'I shall increase and not stray.'

Yet he clung to the evil inclination until the wellsprings of wisdom departed from him. He later returned before his Master, and some were revealed to him, but not as before. h: Malchus, Shabbos and the Oral Torah

p: משא"כ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הִכִּיר כְּלָל בְּמַעֲלַת מַדְרֵגָתוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה רַק הֶחֱזִיק עַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִי' אֱמוּנָה כְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
Moshe Rabbeinu, by contrast, did not consider his exalted station as a personal entitlement. He held himself to be a person of faith like any Israelite.
וזש"נ לֹא כֵן עַבְדִּי מֹשֶׁה בְּכָל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמָן הוּא.
Hence Scripture says: 'Not so My servant Moshe; in all My house he is faithful.'
וְזֶהוּ יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
This explains 'Moshe shall rejoice in the gift of his portion,' the day of Shabbos.
שֶׁבַּחַי' הַשַּׁבָּת דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגְּרָמָהּ כְּלוּם רַק מַה דְּיָהֲבִין לָהּ.
For Shabbos is the aspect that has nothing from itself, possessing only what is given to it.
וְאָמַר הַטַּעַם כִּי עֶבֶד נֶאֱמָן קָרָאתָ לּוֹ דְּאַף שֶׁמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ מְעֻולָּה וְגָבוֹהַּ אַף מִבְּחֵי' אֱמֶת וְכָאָמוּר.
And the reason is given: 'For You called him a faithful servant.' Even though Moshe's station was higher than the attribute of truth, as explained,
מ"מ הוּא לֹא יָדַע מַעֲלָתוֹ וְתָלָה הַכֹּל בִּבְחִירַת השי"ת שֶׁבָּחַר בּוֹ וְנָתַן לוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הַגְּבוֹהוֹת.
he did not claim that rank as his own, but attributed it all to Hashem's choice to select him and confer such high levels upon him.
וְהֶחֱזִיק א"ע רַק בֶּאֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה ועז"נ כִּי עֶבֶד נֶאֱמָן קָרָאתָ לּוֹ.
He considered himself only a person of abundant faith; hence, 'For You called him a faithful servant.'

וְכֵן בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהַיִּשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשֶׂה עָנִי וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרַשׁ פָּסוּק עָנִי וְנַכֵּה רוּחַ וְגוֹ' (בְּרֵישׁ סא"ר) עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז מַכִּיר הֲיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלֵית לֵיהּ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם אָז הַזְּמַן לִזְכּוֹת לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיתָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן כ) וְכֵן עֲנִיָּה אוֹרָיְיתָא דע"פ וַדַּאי וְאִיהִי קַבָּלָה כַּד מְקַבְּלָא מִבַּעַל צְדָקָה דְּאִיהוּ אוֹרָיְיתָא דְּבִכְתָב כַּד אָזְלַת לְגַבֵּיהּ לְקַבָּלָה אִתַּקְּרִיאֵת הֲלָכָה כו' ע"ש.

So on Shabbos a Jew becomes 'poor,' as the verse about 'the poor and contrite in spirit' is interpreted in Seder Eliyahu Rabbah at its beginning concerning Shabbos. For then a Jew recognizes that he possesses nothing of himself. This is the time to merit the Oral Torah. Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 20) calls the Oral Torah 'poor,' receiving from the charitable giver, the Written Torah; when she comes to receive, she is called halachah.
וְזֶהוּ מ"ש מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ:
This is the teaching, 'Malchus is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah.'
